title: Machine-learning force fields: From interatomic forces to material properties
summary: Simulating ion transport in a battery or protein folding requires knowing the forces between atoms. Machine-learning force fields trained on electronic-structure calculations allow more configurations to be explored, but accurately calculating a diffusion coefficient or reaction rate requires accuracy and simulation time suited to that property. Using Kabylda and colleagues’ SO3LR Tauri preprint, released on 4 November 2026, as a recent example, this review follows how energy gradients become forces and how atomic motion yields material properties.
